Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.27. Source: Kubernetes v1.27.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.27.0 / Urgent Upgrade Notes / (No, really, you MUST read this before you upgrade).
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
The in-tree cloud provider for AWS (and the EBS storage plugin) has now been removed. Please use the external cloud provider and CSI driver from https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws instead.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
v1.27.0 / Urgent Upgrade Notes / (No, really, you MUST read this before you upgrade): 'The IPv6DualStack feature gate for external cloud providers was removed. (The feature became GA in 1.23 and the gate was removed for all other components several releases ago.) If you were still manually enabling it you must stop now.' Give terminal phase correctly to all pods that will not be restarted. In particular, assign Failed phase to pods which are deleted while pending. Also, assign a terminal phase (Succeeded or Failed, depending on the exit statuses of the pod containers) to pods which are deleted while running. This fixes the issue for jobs using pod failure policy (with JobPodFailurePolicy and PodDisruptionConditions feature gates enabled) that their pods could get stuck in the pending phase when deleted. Users who maintain controllers which relied on the fact that pods with RestartPolicy=Always never enter the Succeeded phase may need to adapt their controllers. This is because as a consequence of the change pods which use RestartPolicy=Always may end up in the Succeeded phase in two scenarios: pod deletion and graceful node shutdown. The in-tree cloud provider for AWS (and the EBS storage plugin) has now been removed. Please use the external cloud provider and CSI driver from https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws instead.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.27 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: In-tree AWS cloud provider and EBS storage plugin removed
paths.description: The in-tree AWS cloud provider and the in-tree EBS storage plugin were removed in 1.27. Clusters that still depend on them must move to the external cloud-provider-aws and the AWS EBS CSI driver before upgrading to 1.29.

conditions.statement: The upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29 crosses release 1.27, in which the in-tree AWS cloud provider and EBS plugin were removed.
quotes: The in-tree cloud provider for AWS (and the EBS storage plugin) has now been removed.
conditions.relevance: Establishes that the removal took effect in 1.27, which is between the source version 1.23 and target version 1.29.

conditions.statement: The cluster relies on the in-tree AWS cloud provider (e.g. for node lifecycle, load balancers, or routes on AWS).
quotes: The in-tree cloud provider for AWS (and the EBS storage plugin) has now been removed.
conditions.relevance: The in-tree AWS cloud provider no longer exists, so clusters using it lose that functionality unless they switch to the external provider.
ambiguities: The text does not state which specific components, flags or features depend on the in-tree provider.

conditions.statement: Workloads or StorageClasses use the in-tree EBS storage plugin (kubernetes.io/aws-ebs, awsElasticBlockStore volumes).
quotes: The in-tree cloud provider for AWS (and the EBS storage plugin) has now been removed.
conditions.relevance: The EBS storage plugin was removed, so volumes and StorageClasses using the in-tree plugin are affected unless moved to the CSI driver.
ambiguities: The text does not name the literal provisioner or volume source identifiers; they are inferred from the EBS plugin name.

suggested_actions: Use the external cloud provider and CSI driver from https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws instead.
Before upgrading, inventory clusters, StorageClasses, and PersistentVolumes that rely on the in-tree AWS provider or EBS plugin and plan migration to the external cloud provider and CSI driver.
